UNITED STATES ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY WASHINGTON, D.C. 20460
4 FEB 1975
OFFICE OF THE ADMINISTRATOR
Mr. John P. Giacomini National Science Foundation Room 701 1800 G Street, N.W. Washington, D.C.
Dear Mr. Giacomini:
The Environmental Protection Agency has reviewed the draft environmental impact statement on the Ross Ice Shelf Project (RISP), U.S. Antarctic Research Program, issued by the National Science Foundation on October 25, 1974. We offer the following comments for your consideration in preparing the final statement.
General Comments
It appears that two-thirds of the project will have been completed prior to the issuance of the final environmental statement. Nevertheless, we believe that to assist our review of project plans not yet undertaken, more specific details on work already completed should be included in the final statement. In addition, a glossary covering the technical terms used in the draft statement should be provided. This will facilitate public understanding of the project and its impacts and should enhance the readability of the final statement.
We also suggest that a small radiological study be incorporated into the project plan. EPA is currently supporting a research investigation designed to study various glacier environments for heavy metals and a number of radionuclides to determine the impact on the environment from activities which release radioactive effluents to the atmosphere.
